answer: We cannot yet recommend a product to buy, because the enquiry does not name the product, the quality attribute to monitor or the sample state. AFS's pathway starts with multi-method lab trials on your own process before choosing a system, and NIR fiber-probe spectroscopy is the first method to test because it is the most common online method (S01-3-unknown, S05-pathway, S01-10-nir).

inline.headline: Test NIR fiber-probe spectroscopy on your product in a lab trial before buying any instrument
inline.probe: NIR diffuse reflection probe for opaque or scattering samples, or NIR transmission/transflection probe for clear liquids, chosen by sample type
inline.install: At the product stream where the quality is to be monitored; the exact location is not yet known, so start with bench samples
inline.test_against: MIR ATR probe on the same samples
inline.not_final_because: The product, quality attribute and sample state are unknown, NIR needs chemometric calibration built and validated on your samples, and the silica fiber's 2400 nm upper limit is below the 2500 nm upper end of the NIR range.

problems.text: AI cannot monitor product quality by itself; it needs a spectral sensor and a chemometric model that is built, validated and then applied to the process.
Buying an instrument before the target is defined risks choosing a method that cannot see the quality attribute, because no single method suits every sample.
The NIR range of 780-2500 nm extends above the 2400 nm upper limit of the Vis-NIR silica fiber, so the fiber and the spectrometer range must be checked against the method.
Quality of the product is not defined in measurable terms; a model needs independent laboratory reference values for the quality attribute to be calibrated and validated.

methods.why: It is the most common online fiber-probe method and penetrates up to several millimetres, but its broad overlapping bands require chemometrics.
It carries information complementary to MIR and gives molecular detail, but its signal is weak and can be masked by fluorescence, so special probes are needed.
Its absorption peaks are well defined and selective, but it is limited to thin layers and liquids or soft solids at the ATR contact, and its cost is high.
It is highly sensitive, but most chemicals do not fluoresce, so it is useful only if the product has a fluorescent component.

questions.q: Which product, and which quality attribute (for example concentration, moisture or fat) must the monitoring measure, and what accuracy is needed?
questions.why: The attribute decides the method, and no method can be selected or tested without it.

questions.q: What is the sample state (clear liquid, thick or opaque, paste, powder or solid), and where in the process would the probe sit?
questions.why: The sample state decides the probe type and whether transmission or reflection can be used, since transmission fails in thick or opaque media.

questions.q: Do you have a reference laboratory method and samples with known values for the quality attribute?
questions.why: Calibration and validation need independent laboratory reference values.

questions.q: Does the product contain a fluorescent component, and is it homogeneous across the sampled spot?
questions.why: A fluorescent component makes fluorescence worth testing, and heterogeneity means the methods must see the same spot.

experiment.objective: Compare NIR, Raman and MIR ATR on representative product samples and identify which method, or fused pair, best separates the quality classes on independent validation data.
steps: Collect product samples across the expected quality range and obtain independent laboratory reference values for the quality attribute.
Record spectra with NIR, Raman and MIR ATR on the same samples, using fiber probes that cover each method's range.
Build a chemometric model per method on a calibration set and test each on a separate validation set.
Build a fused NIR + Raman model from synchronised spectra and compare it with the best single method on the same validation data.
Identify the key spectral features behind the chosen model and report which method performed best.

pathway.key_features: Not yet identified; they must be found by multivariate analysis of the lab-trial spectra.
pathway.path_reason: The product, quality attribute and sample state are not known, so no tailored solution can be chosen before the lab test.

multispectral.why: NIR responds to hydrogen bonds and polar groups while Raman responds to the molecular backbone and non-polar groups, so their information is complementary.
multispectral.test: Compare the fused NIR + Raman model with the best single-method model on the same independent validation samples, and keep the combination only if it beats that single method.

assumptions: The product, the quality attribute and the sample state are undefined and are not assumed.
A remote fiber probe is assumed to be possible at the process, since the client did not state otherwise.
No spectra, accuracy, detection limits or prices were supplied, so none are given.
NIR is the first test because it is the most common online fiber-probe method, not because the product is known to suit it.
AI is taken to mean a chemometric or machine-learning model applied to spectra.
